children: U.S. natural gas futures fall for a second consecutive session as the market looks beyond this week's inventory report to cooler weather that's likely to cut demand heading into the shoulder season. The EIA is expected to report a 28 Bcf increase in underground storage for last week, according to a WSJ survey of analysts. That's smaller than the average 52 Bcf injection and would reduce the inventory surplus over the average to 136 Bcf from 160 Bcf the week before. Nymex natural gas settles down 3.2% at $2.822/mmBtu.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
